question.problem: The first term of a geometric sequence is $1,$ and the common ratio is $-2.$ The $6$th term of this sequence is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The first term is ${a}_{1}=1,$ and the common ratio is $r=-2,$ so we can write the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =1\cdot (-2)^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the $6$th term, we can use this formula with $n=6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =1\cdot (-2)^{n-1} \\ {a}_{6} & =1\cdot (-2)^{6-1} \\  & =1\cdot (-2)^{5} \\  & =1\cdot (-32) \\  & =-32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $6$th term is ${a}_{6}=-32.$
